newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies close sharply higher, hogs mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies close sharply higher, hogs mixed.

text.p: CME pork belly futures closed sharply higher after being up as much as the 2.000 cent daily limit in late trade on support from strong technicals and firmer cash. Hogs finished mixed with nearbys up on strong cash ideas, traders said.
February bellies bulged the daily limit to 79.550 cents per lb late before profit taking pared gains and prices closed 1.425 to 0.100 higher. February was up most at 78.975 cents.
Pork belly trade was very erratic early but prices rallied when commercial buying prompted by firmer cash touched off technical buy stops, traders said.

Technical stops were touched off in February above 78.200 cents early and again above 78.900 cents late. Bellies had posted sharp early gains on carryover technical support and were drifting back before midsession on profit taking before the commercial buying again turned prices higher, they said.

Movement of product appears to have increased at the lower price levels and there are reports of increased movement of frozen product. Increased belly demand came despite a rising hog slaughter rate, they said.
R.J. O'Brien was a notable buyer on the late rally, pit sources said.

Fund rolling by Refco, selling October and buying December, again pared the gain in October hog futures late. That month had moved higher again after a round of profit-taking near midsession and set a new session as well as one-month high before slipping at the close, traders said.

Expectations of higher cash hog markets into the weekend and strong pork demand prompted buying. Packers are expected to slaughter heavily on Saturday. Export demand for pork appears to be rising and increased domestic pork featuring is seen going into October, National Pork Month, they said.
Rand Financials was notably a net buyer in October and December and Cargill Investor Services bought December late, pit sources said.

In hog options, Lind-Waldock notably bought February 66 to 74 puts early. R.J. O'Brien sold February 70 puts and other wire houses followed. They also sold April 74 calls. Volatility was firmer, pit sources added.
Hog futures closed 0.525 cent higher to 0.350 lower with October up 0.500 at 55.400 cents.
